# Power monitor / distribution - BOM (rev 0, draft)

Written 2026-11-14. Status: DRAFT, not ordered.

**Schematics + authoritative BOM are now in `kicad/`** (generated by
`kicad/gen_schematic.py`, KiCad 8 format):
- `main_board.kicad_sch`, `ct_board.kicad_sch` - open in KiCad 8, 9 or 10.
  Design calculations are written on the sheets as text blocks.
- `main_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv`, `ct_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv` - JLCPCB BOM
  (`kicad/export_bom.py` regenerates them). Every LCSC number was checked
  for stock on 2026-11-14.
- `PowerMonitor.pretty/` + `fp-lib-table` - project footprints: ZMCT103C,
  single Keystone 3557 fuse clip (two per fuse), Kinghelm RJ45 with shield-tab slots.
- `main_board.kicad_pcb`, `ct_board.kicad_pcb` - footprints PLACED, not routed
  (`kicad/gen_pcb.py`, 100 x 100 mm and 100 x 30 mm). 3D models: KiCad 10
  library STEP via `${KICAD10_3DMODEL_DIR}`, ZMCT103C vendor STEP and a simple
  Keystone 3557 clip body in `kicad/PowerMonitor.3dshapes/`. Nets come from the
  schematic and footprints are linked by symbol UUID, so KiCad "Update PCB
  from Schematic" matches them. Re-running gen_pcb.py overwrites the board -
  stop once parts are moved / routed by hand in KiCad.
- `netcheck.py` - netlist extractor used to prove re-layouts keep connectivity.
- `../design_calcs.py` -> `../CALCULATIONS.txt` - all calculations, with the
  datasheet values they use.
The tables below are the design notes; where they differ, the schematic wins.

Changes made while drawing the schematic (2026-11-14):
- MCU: **STM32G071KBT6** (LQFP-32, LCSC C529348, only ~200 in stock - order
  early). The KBT6N (C529349) is out of stock. KBT6 is the "GP" pinout and
  KBT6N the "PD" pinout (DS12232 Rev 3 fig. 7). They differ on pins 17 and
  26-29 only, so the schematic uses a modified symbol
  (PowerMonitor:STM32G071KBTx). The status LED moves from PB15 to PB2.
  VDD = VDDA on this package -> one ferrite (FB1) feeds the whole MCU.
  Pin map: PA0 = V, PA1 / PB0 / PB1 / PA7 = CT1-CT4 (all FT_a pins), PB6/PB7 = I2C1
  SCL/SDA, PA8 = CRITICAL (open-drain), PB2 = status LED, PB8 = heater
  relay enable, PA13/PA14 = SWD, PF2 = NRST. Pull-ups on PA3, PA10
  (bootloader USART RX) and PA4 (SPI1 NSS). **Checked against AN2606 Rev 62
  table 91** (see "Datasheet review" below).
- Fuse holders: Keystone 3568 is out of stock, so each fuse sits in **2x
  Keystone 3557** single clips (C2680614, 14 clips in total). Each clip has
  its own designator (F1A/F1B ... F7A/F7B) because JLC places one part per
  designator. Layout: the two clips of a fuse go 9.73 mm apart centre to
  centre, legs in line (Keystone layout, 3.40 mm leg spacing, 1.6 mm holes);
  the footprint's F.Fab layer shows the mating clip position.
  The clips are bare metal, so keep 24 V copper and other parts clear.
- 24 V input terminal: same 5.08 mm 18 A terminal as the outputs (no 7.62 mm
  2-pin footprint in the KiCad library; max input current ~8.5 A).
- Bias 1.65 V: one shared divider (R70/R71 + C30/C31) for all 5 channels.
- Footprints checked against the drawings:
  - RJ45 Kinghelm KH-RJ45-58 is the KiCad Amphenol 54602 grid plus 2 plated
    shield-tab slots (tabs 15.13 mm apart, 4.95 mm from the front edge), with
    a 0.9 mm pin drill.
  - Barrel jack CUI PJ-002AH (C2961147) = KiCad BarrelJack_Horizontal.
  - ZMCT103C: custom (pins 0.9 mm on an 11.8 mm pitch, body 18.2 x 10.2 mm).
- Parts replaced because they were out of stock:
  - shunts YAGEO PA2512 10m (C375688), FOJAN FRM252 20m/50m (C7420049/C7420008)
  - SMBJ24A Littelfuse (C224017)
  - ferrite Murata BLM18KG601 (C85833)
  - J11 JST B2B-XH-A (C158012)
- 100 nF: C14663 is out of stock at LCSC -> all 15 now C346191 (Samsung
  CL10B104KB8NFNC, 50 V X7R, in stock).
- Datasheet review changes: INA filter R 10 -> 1 Ohm, CT burden -> 49.9 Ohm,
  AC divider 100k -> 120k, PB9 pull-up removed, 100k on each CT input. See
  CALCULATIONS.txt.
- Added the heater safety relay driver (block G): Q1 (STM32 PB8) AND Q2 (Pi,
  J10 pin 6) in series, flyback SS14, 1 A fuse, LED, 24 V coil on J12.

Independent design review (2026-11-14) - fixed:
- **BAV99 clamps D10-D14 were reversed** (shorted 3V3 to GND through two
  diodes). The KiCad 8 BAV99 symbol pin NAMES are wrong; pin numbers follow
  the datasheet: 1 = A1 -> GND, 2 = K2 -> 3V3, 3 = K1/A2 -> signal.
- CT4 moved from PA5 (TT_a, no positive injection allowed) to PA7 (FT_a,
  ADC_IN7). Anti-alias R 1k -> 2.2k: CT fault current 6.75 -> 3.1 mA (the old
  calculation had a sign error). fc 7.2 kHz, 0.40 deg at 50 Hz.
- RS2 (Spider, 10 A fuse) 10 -> 5 mOhm (Milliohm C5375417): at 1.35x fuse
  rating (may flow up to 30 min) 10 mOhm was 1.82 W on a 2 W part.
- Fuse clips split into one designator per clip (see above).
- D2 SMBJ5.0A -> SMBJ6.0A (MDD C113976): VRWM 6 V above the 5.25 V Pi supply.
- PWR_FLAG on 5V_BUS (ERC: U12 VIN is power_in, fed through RS8).
- ZMCT103C symbol without the non-existent primary pins (no "pad not found").
- JP1 / J22 excluded from the JLC BOM (copper jumper / hand-soldered header).
- **BOOT0 jumper JP1 only works after nBOOT_SEL = 0** is written to the option
  bytes; factory value 1 = BOOT0 pin ignored (AN2606 pattern 11). Write it on
  the first SWD flash, otherwise SWD (connect under reset) is the recovery.
Open from the review:
- **No reverse-polarity protection on J1/J2**: a reversed input kills U1-U3
  (IN+- min -0.3 V). Options: polarized connector (e.g. XT60) or a P-FET.
- RJ45 footprint still to be checked against the Kinghelm drawing / part.

## Concept - two boards
| | **CT board** (in the mains area) | **Main board** (next to the Pi) |
|---|---|---|
| Where | Electronics bay, next to the AC inlet / SSRs / PSU | Electronics bay, next to the Pi |
| What | 4 wire-through current transformers + burden resistors + clamps | STM32G071 (mains V/I/W), 3 x INA3221 (24 V / 5 V), fused 24 V / 5 V distribution |
| Mains copper | **None** - mains wires only pass through the CT holes | None - mains voltage via an external AC-AC adapter |
| Link | RJ45 <- shielded Cat6 STP (4 twisted pairs = 4 CTs), <= 1 m -> RJ45 | |

- The Pi reads everything over one I2C bus (`dtparam=i2c_arm=on` is
  already set): INA3221 at 0x40-0x42, STM32G071 as I2C target at 0x50.
- Board 3.3 V from its own LDO (fed from the 5 V input).

## Board 1: CT board

| CT ch | Mains load | Expected max | Burden | Signal at max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CT1 | Printer total (mains in) | ~6.3 A | 49.9 Ohm | 0.31 V rms |
| CT2 | Bed heater (750 W) | 3.3 A | 49.9 Ohm | 0.17 V rms |
| CT3 | Chamber heater (<= 500 W, cold inrush higher) | 2.2 A | 49.9 Ohm | 0.11 V rms |
| CT4 | Spare (future 48 V motor PSU, LRS-200 primary, ...) | - | 49.9 Ohm | - |

Alternative checked 2026-11-14: ZHT ZHT103 (C2935356, ~$0.25 vs $0.26) - not used:
specified at a 100 Ohm burden, class 0.5 (vs 0.2 %), phase <= 30' (vs 15'), linear
0-10 A (vs 0-15 A), 3200 V isolation (vs 4500 V), 12.0 mm pin pitch (footprint
change), 2.3k in stock vs 17k. Saving ~3 cents per board.

49.9 Ohm on all four: the ZMCT103C datasheet specifies accuracy (0.2 %),
phase error (<= 15') and the 0-15 A linear range at a 50 Ohm burden. The
first draft used 100/150 Ohm, which is outside the specified conditions.
Clipping is at ~22 A rms, 1 ADC LSB = 16 mA, and the RMS over 800 samples
resolves well below that (see CALCULATIONS.txt).

Parts: see `kicad/ct_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv` (ZMCT103C, 49.9 Ohm 0.1 %
burden at the CT pins, SMAJ5.0CA across each burden, shielded RJ45, M3
holes) plus cable-tie slots next to each CT for strain relief.

### CT board layout and safety rules
- **No copper except the CT secondaries, burdens, TVS and RJ45.** A routed
  slot / keep-out around each CT hole.
- The CT hole is only **5 mm**: one single conductor (the L wire of that
  load, H07V-K / silicone 1.5 mm2, ~3-3.5 mm OD) goes through each CT, not
  a whole cable. Add a thin silicone or heat-shrink sleeve over that wire
  as the second insulation layer (OD must stay < 5 mm), strain-relieve it
  with cable ties so it cannot slide or touch anything else.
- All CTs threaded the same direction (P1* side = supply side, marked on
  the silkscreen), otherwise the power sign flips (firmware can correct it).
- CT isolation rating assumes intact wire insulation - do not thread bare or
  damaged wire.
- RJ45 shield connected to GND on the main board only (one end).
- 230 V wiring done by someone used to mains wiring.

## Board 2: Main board

### Channel map, DC side (proposal - adjust before layout)
INA3221 shunt full scale 163.84 mV, LSB 40 uV.

| Chip / addr | Ch | Rail / load | Expected max | Fuse | Shunt | Full scale | LSB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 / 0x40 (A0=GND) | 1 | **24 V input** from LRS-200-24 | 8.5 A | - (PSU side) | 10 mOhm | 16.4 A | 4 mA |
| U1 | 2 | 24 V -> Spider (motors + logic + its fans) | 7 A | 10 A | 5 mOhm | 32.8 A | 8 mA |
| U1 | 3 | 24 V -> SB2040 (hotend + toolhead fans) | 3.5 A | 5 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U2 / 0x41 (A0=VS) | 1 | 24 V -> chamber heater fan(s) / bed fans | 1.5 A | 3 A | 50 mOhm | 3.3 A | 0.8 mA |
| U2 | 2 | 24 V -> Nevermore / exhaust | 1.5 A | 3 A | 50 mOhm | 3.3 A | 0.8 mA |
| U2 | 3 | 24 V -> lights (Daylight XXL) | 2 A | 3 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U3 / 0x42 (A0=SDA) | 1 | 24 V -> spare (12 V buck for the PTC fan, ...) | 2 A | 3 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |
| U3 | 2 | **5 V input** (today: Spider 5 V pin; later a dedicated 5 V supply) | 4 A | - | 10 mOhm | 16.4 A | 4 mA |
| U3 | 3 | 5 V -> Pi (+ screen, USB cam via Pi) | 3.5 A | 5 A | 20 mOhm | 8.2 A | 2 mA |

Fan channels use 50 mOhm so a stalled or dead fan (~0.1 A drop) is clearly
visible. Sum check: 24 V input vs. sum of the 24 V outputs.

#### INA3221 26 V limit - mitigation
The INA3221 input common-mode range (and abs max) is 26 V, only ~2 V above
the 24 V rail:
- Set the LRS-200-24 output to 24.0 V (adjustable 21.6-28.8 V), check with
  a multimeter.
- The board sits on the PSU side; motor braking spikes are mostly absorbed
  by the Spider's own bulk capacitors.
- Input RC filter on every channel, bulk capacitance and TVS on the 24 V
  bus (the TVS only catches large spikes - it clamps above 26 V).
- If the rail ever needs to go above 24 V: INA237 (85 V, in stock) or INA228, rev 1.

### Mains side (signals from the CT board + AC adapter)
**MCU: STM32G071KBT6** (LQFP-32, GP pinout, 128 KB flash, 12-bit ADC up to 2.5 Msps,
hardware oversampling, internal oscillator - no crystal or external flash).
Samples 4 CT channels + mains voltage at ~4 kHz each; over 10 cycles
(200 ms) computes Vrms, Irms, real power (W), VA, power factor, Hz and
accumulates Wh per channel. Multiplexed sampling (~1 us apart) gives
< 0.1 degree phase error at 50 Hz - negligible.

**Mains voltage (230 V / 50 Hz) without mains on the PCB:** an external
AC-AC wall adapter (transformer type, 9-12 V **AC** output - not a DC
adapter). Its output is divided down and biased to 1.65 V (OpenEnergyMonitor
emonTx method). Calibrate once against a multimeter.

**Firmware updates from the Pi, no extra wires:** the STM32G0 ROM bootloader
supports I2C1 (AN2606). The application implements a "jump to bootloader"
I2C command; the Pi then flashes over the same bus (`stm32flash` supports
I2C). A blank chip starts the bootloader by itself (empty-flash check).
Recovery: SWD header (ST-Link, or OpenOCD on Pi GPIOs, connect under reset)
and a BOOT0 solder pad that only works once nBOOT_SEL = 0. Notes:
- Use **I2C1 on the pins AN2606 lists for the G07x bootloader** for the
  target interface, so app and bootloader share the bus pins (verify in
  AN2606 before layout).
- Check that the bootloader's fixed I2C address does not collide with
  0x40-0x42 / 0x50 (AN2606).
- Known issue (ST community): G07x/G08x bootloader **V11.3** can get stuck
  polling USART3 while the host uses I2C, stretching SCL. Mitigation: pull-ups
  on all bootloader USART RX pins so they idle high, and keep SWD as fallback.
- BOOT0 is PA14 = SWCLK on the G0 (shared pin); boot selection via option
  bytes. Factory nBOOT_SEL = 1 means the BOOT0 pin is ignored (AN2606
  pattern 11): write nBOOT_SEL = 0 on the first SWD flash to make JP1 work.
  Do not hard-wire PA14.

### Main board components
The full part list with values, footprints and LCSC numbers is
`kicad/main_board_bom_jlcpcb.csv` (generated from the schematic). Off the
JLC BOM: JP1 (solder jumper, copper only), J22 (SWD header, hand-soldered),
test points and mounting holes; the 7 ATM fuses are bought separately
(10 A x1, 5 A x2, 3 A x4).

INA address pins hard-wired: U1 A0->GND (0x40), U2 A0->VS (0x41), U3
A0->SDA (0x42). 0x43 free. INA PV and TC outputs unused (open-drain, NC).

### Main board PCB
- 2 layers, **2 oz copper**, approx. 110 x 90 mm.
- 24 V bus and the input/Spider paths: wide pours on both layers, stitching
  vias (>= 10 A).
- **Kelvin connections** from the inner ends of each shunt pad, routed as a
  pair to the RC filter and the INA.
- Analog section (RJ45, bias, anti-alias, MCU ADC pins) in a separate corner
  away from the high-current pours and fuses; solid GND plane underneath.
- Silkscreen: channel names, fuse ratings, polarity, "24.0 V MAX".

## Software (to do)
- STM32G071 firmware: ADC + DMA at ~4 kHz per channel, RMS/power math over
  10 cycles, I2C target 0x50 with a register map (V, I, W, VA, PF, Hz, Wh
  per channel) and a "jump to bootloader" command.
- Python service on the Pi: reads the 3 INA3221 (0x40-0x42) and the
  STM32 (0x50), publishes to Moonraker (MQTT sensor component) for history
  and Mainsail.
- Checks: 24 V input vs. sum of outputs; fan channel current too low ->
  warning; bed/chamber current while Klipper reports the heater off -> stuck
  SSR -> open the heater safety relay/contactor (normally open, actively held on).

## Alert handling - all options available
CRITICAL and WARNING are open-drain, wired-OR lines, so they can go to
several inputs at once. The board supports every reaction; which one is
used is chosen in software/config, not by rewiring:

| Source | Line | Goes to | Possible reaction (configurable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| INA3221 critical limit (per channel, hardware comparator, ~1 ms) | CRITICAL | Spider input (J11) **and** Pi GPIO (J10) | Klipper `[gcode_button]` on the Spider pin: `PAUSE`, `M112` (emergency stop) or log only |
| INA3221 warning limit (averaged) | WARNING | Pi GPIO (J10) | Pi service: log / Mainsail notification / Mobileraker push |
| STM32 mains checks (overcurrent, bed/chamber current outside expected range) | CRITICAL (open-drain GPIO) | same as above | same as above - works even if the Pi service is not running |
| Pi service (stuck SSR: current while Klipper reports heater off) | - (software) | Moonraker `[power]` (gpio) | open the heater safety relay/contactor, `M112` via Moonraker |

Limits for the INA critical/warning comparators and the STM32 checks are
written over I2C by the Pi service at start-up (stored in a config file),
so they can be changed without reflashing.

## 5 V supply note
Today the Pi is fed from the Spider's 5 V pin. The board measures whatever
feeds the 5 V input, so nothing changes in the design. Recommended later:
a dedicated 5 V supply (e.g. Mean Well LRS-35-5 / LRS-50-5 or a 24 V -> 5 V
5 A DIN buck) into the 5 V input - takes the Pi + screen + USB cam load off
the Spider's regulator and avoids Pi brown-outs.

## Alternatives considered for the DC monitor (2026-11-14)
| Option | ICs + decoupling for 9 ch | Bus max | Resolution / offset | LCSC (price, stock) | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **TI INA3221** (chosen) | 3 + 3 | 26 V | 40 uV LSB, 80 uV max | C181255, ~$1.33, 5.6k | Fewest parts, 4 addresses = 12 ch max |
| TI INA226, 1 ch | 9 + 9 | 36 V | 2.5 uV LSB, 10 uV max | C49851, ~$0.38, 61k | Better accuracy and 36 V headroom, but +12 parts and 9 alert lines |
| 3PEAK TPA626 (Chinese, INA226 pin/register compatible) | 9 + 9 | 36 V | as INA226 | C5761471, ~$0.50, JLC Extended | Same as INA226, no real gain |
| TI INA219 | 9 + 9 | 26 V | 10 uV LSB, 12-bit | C138706, ~$0.49 | Same 26 V limit, worse ADC - no |
| TI INA237, 1 ch | 9 + 9 | 85 V | 5 uV LSB, 50 uV max, gain 0.3 % | C2864837, ~$1.07, 7.0k | Best choice for a 48 V variant |
| TI INA228 / INA238, 1 ch | 9 + 9 | 85 V | 20-bit / 16-bit | C2887910 / C2868250, out of stock | INA228 would be ideal (energy) when back |
| TI INA4230 / INA4235, 4 ch 48 V | 3 + 3 | 48 V | 16-bit | C41348431 (20 pcs) / C33440856 (207 pcs), ~$5, DSBGA only | Not hand/inspection friendly, low stock - no |

What each part computes on-chip (TI product pages, INA3221 SBOS576C):

| Part | Shunt + bus V | Current | Power | Energy / charge | Die temp | Alerts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| INA3221 | yes | - | - | - | - | Critical (per conversion, per channel), Warning (averaged, per channel), shunt-sum limit, PV (all rails above limit), each on its own pin |
| INA226 / TPA626 / INA219 | yes | yes | yes | - | - | 1 pin, one selectable limit (INA219: none) |
| INA237 / INA238 | yes | yes | yes | - | yes | 1 pin, several limits (V, I, P, temp), 75 us response |
| INA228 | yes | yes | yes | yes / yes | yes | as INA237 + shunt tempco compensation |
| INA4235 | yes | yes | yes | yes / - | - | over/under current and voltage per channel |

Current and power on-chip are only a convenience here: the host computes
I = Vshunt / Rshunt and P = Vbus x I in one line, with the same accuracy (the
bus is a stiff 24 V). On-chip energy accumulation (INA228, INA4235) is the one
real gain: it integrates every conversion, while the INA3221 multiplexes 6
measurements, so each channel is sampled ~1/6 of the time. With on-chip
averaging and 1 s polling the per-print energy error is a few percent, which is
enough for this board. The INA3221 has the best alert set: CRITICAL is wired
to the STM32 (PA8), the Pi (J10 pin 4) and a Spider input (J11), WARNING to the
Pi (J10 pin 5); PV is unused.

A 48 V variant of this board is not planned (decided 2026-11-14): on printers
that use 48 V, only the stepper drivers get it, from a separate PSU. If that
PSU is added, its mains input is measured on CT4 (spare) instead - real power
in W including the PSU losses, no DC parts on the board change. The 24 V side
stays INA3221.

No Chinese INA3221 equivalent was found (3PEAK, SGMICRO, lingxingic only
clone the single-channel / analog INA parts). The INA226/TPA626 route only
pays off if the 24 V rail must ever run above ~25 V; until then the
INA3221 keeps the board smallest.

## Decisions
- 2026-11-14: no Shelly. Heater cut-off is a mechanical relay/contactor (NO, coil held on, cuts only the heater supply), not an SSR - an SSR usually fails shorted.
- 2026-11-14: mains voltage measured via AC-AC adapter (230 V / 50 Hz).
- 2026-11-14: two boards (CT board + main board), STM32G071 instead of RP2350B.
- 2026-11-14: JLCPCB assembly (prefer Basic parts).
- 2026-11-14: all alert reactions supported (log / pause / emergency stop / heater relay cut), chosen in config.

## Open
- Channel map: which loads are actually wired separately today (check the
  electronics bay)? Is the Pi fed from its own 5 V PSU or a buck?
- Dedicated 5 V supply for the Pi: which one (see 5 V supply note)?
- Heater relay/contactor: pick a 24 V coil, NO contacts rated for the heater
  (230 V, >= 10 A resistive), coil <= 0.5 A.
- Pi GPIO for HEATER_EN_PI: use one >= GPIO9 (pulled low at boot), e.g. GPIO22.
